java_model: PSystemBuilder tries SequenceDiagramFactory before ClassDiagramFactory, then Activity, Description, and the later UML factories for @startuml sources.

PSystemCommandFactory.getCandidate first tests a single line. If a command returns OK_PARTIAL, isMultilineCommandOk accumulates physical lines into one BlocLines value until that same command returns OK or NOT_OK.
CommandMultilines2 matches only the first line against the starting regex while the final line must match the command's end regex; interior lines are command payload.
CommandFactoryNote accepts `note as CODE ... end note` as a Class command, and CommandFactoryNoteOnEntity accepts both `note ... end note` and bracket-terminated `note ... { ... }` attached forms.
SequenceDiagramFactory registers multiline `note`, `hnote`, and `rnote` commands; their terminators include `end note`, `end hnote`, and `end rnote` depending on the form.
rust_model: detect_uml_subtype now computes completed_multiline_note_payload and skips lines marked as payload before applying subtype heuristics.

completed_multiline_note_payload recognizes only openers whose first whitespace token equals `note`, excludes colon and quoted single-line forms, and hides through a later case-insensitive `end note` terminator.

The opener line remains visible to scoring. Mixed-case `NoTe as ...` is not counted as class evidence by the later subtype heuristics, so an otherwise note-only diagram can fall back to the default SEQUENCE subtype.
Bracket-terminated attached notes, `hnote`, and `rnote` are outside the current span detector even though Java accepts them as multiline commands.

perturbations.failure_summary: Java renders CLASS with an attached note. Rust renders SEQUENCE, creating participant data from note-body words such as `remains`.
Java command regexes accept the mixed-case note block as CLASS. Rust hides the payload but does not count the mixed-case opener as class evidence, so it falls back to SEQUENCE.

axes: quoted inline note before multiline note

perturbations.failure_summary: Both sides render CLASS, but the no-oracle SVG differs in floating-note/class placement. This is a valid held-out failure adjacent to the same multiline note block family.

Java DESCRIPTION keeps the note entity and then renders the node command. Rust selects DESCRIPTION but the deployment parser consumes the note body as a `control` entity named `body`, so subtype isolation alone is insufficient.
Java renders the multiline hnote. Rust stays SEQUENCE but omits the note block, producing a shorter lifeline diagram.
Java renders the multiline rnote. Rust stays SEQUENCE but omits the note block, producing a shorter lifeline diagram.

invalid_probes.observation: Java emitted an error page for an unterminated `note as ...` block, so this was not committed as a valid held-out. It supports the account boundary that unterminated spans must not hide arbitrary later source.

findings: The Java source inspection supports the narrow claim that completed `note ... end note` interiors are accumulated as command payload before factory selection proceeds.

The five preserved note-only failures from the prior SVG logical monospace review now pass under `target/release/examples/diff_one --no-oracle`, so c2aa2daa fixed that exact `note as ... end note` body-keyword leak.

The implementation is too narrow for Java's multiline-note grammar. Java-valid bracket-terminated attached notes are not hidden by `completed_multiline_note_payload`, and fresh `checker_attached_brace_payload_keywords.puml` changes from Java CLASS to Rust SEQUENCE.

The implementation leaves mixed-case note openers under-modeled. Java accepts mixed-case command regexes, but fresh `checker_floating_mixed_case_colored.puml` falls back to Rust SEQUENCE because the opener is not scored as class evidence.

Subtype isolation alone does not preserve Java's model when a note block precedes a DESCRIPTION command: fresh `checker_post_terminator_deployment_visible.puml` selects DESCRIPTION but Rust's deployment parser consumes note payload as a top-level control entity.
Sequence multiline note forms remain incomplete for `hnote` and `rnote`: fresh Java-valid sequence held-outs stay SEQUENCE in Rust but drop the note block, failing no-oracle comparison.
No fixture-shaped product logic or golden-output dependency was found in c2aa2daa for this mechanism.
verdict_reason: Rejected. The old counterexamples pass, but fresh valid held-outs disprove the claimed grammar boundary across bracket-terminated attached notes, mixed-case note commands, DESCRIPTION note consumption before post-terminator commands, and sequence `hnote`/`rnote` forms. Under the T14 held-out rule, any failing valid held-out rejects the implementation.
